analysis.title: US Equity Strategy Weekly Warm-up: Enter Sandman
key_insights: MS says the correction that began in June is in its final phase. The S&P 500 is catching down toward improved breadth. Since September the equal-weight S&P has outperformed the cap-weighted S&P by about 6% and the Russell 2000 by about 4%.

MS wants either more confirmation from its Market Sentiment Indicator or the S&P 500 reaching its tactical downside target of 7100-7300 before adding risk more aggressively. The year-end base case stays at 8000 for the S&P 500.

Since the end of September, 10-year Treasury yields fell nearly 40bp and the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day moving average rose about 20 points to 62%. The equal-weight S&P gained nearly 5%, beating the cap-weighted index by almost 6%.

Damage has been worst in early-cycle groups: Semiconductors, Capital Goods, Transports, Banks and Retailers have fallen materially from summer peaks. Still-crowded areas such as parts of cyclical tech are now catching down, which MS treats as part of the capitulation process.

Fed Chair Warsh acknowledged some tightening in financial conditions but distinguished between conditions being 'tighter' and actually 'tight'. MS reads this as the Fed having room to pause, with a high bar for more liquidity support. Last week's FOMC was not a full clearing event for liquidity.

The Treasury General Account rose about $244B since mid-July while bank reserves fell $249B and Fed assets were roughly unchanged. Treasury projects a TGA peak near $1.05T in late October, falling to about $850B by year-end. A drawdown could ease liquidity, and the Quarterly Refunding Announcement this week is important for back-end issuance.

If the TGA drawdown does not come with looser financial conditions across rates and energy, MS says markets may need more liquidity from the Fed. It asks whether any Fed response would be orderly like last year or disruptive like 2018.

Since 1982, large caps gained about 15% cap-weighted and 16% equal-weighted in the six months after midterms, and about 22% in the following year. Investors already expect a Democrat sweep through a narrow Senate majority, so it is unlikely to be a major surprise.

Most market-moving policies (tariffs, foreign policy, agency-led deregulation) remain under executive control. MS sees the larger risk after the election as renewed military escalation with Iran or new tariffs, especially if higher energy prices lift inflation expectations and long-end yields.

Possible upside from a Democrat majority includes efforts to delay or reverse Medicaid and SNAP cuts, which could support consumption, and a different 2028 policy outlook could pull forward investment and M&A. Opposition to data center development is driven more by local incumbent dynamics than party.

Recent pressure on the cap-weighted index came from AI capex pace, credit spread widening in parts of the AI trade, tighter liquidity, Middle East uncertainty and the midterms. MS reads the credit moves as greater issuer differentiation, not a broad credit problem, and says IG demand is solid and hyperscaler supply is a small share.

In 3Q26, free cash flow surprises are driving larger next-day price reactions than EPS surprises, and FCF misses are punished more heavily than usual. MS reads this as a mid-to-late-cycle market that favors cash conversion and earnings durability, supporting quality cyclicals with improving revisions. Industrials remains the top pick.

60% of Russell 3000 stocks have had at least a 20% correction since June, and the S&P 500 P/E multiple is down 20% from its high a year ago. MS says upcoming clearing events should offer a chance to add risk in quality cyclicals that have de-rated.

3Q26 earnings season: median T+1 price reaction is +0.1% absolute and +0.4% relative, EPS surprise is 3.9% (historical average 4.4%), and sales surprise is 2.0% (historical average 1.3%). 297 of 493 S&P 500 companies have reported. 3Q EPS is expected at +28% y/y and sales at +12% y/y.

Earnings revisions breadth is +7%, lower than the prior six-month level, which MS takes to mean 2027 upward revisions slowed this quarter. Calendar 2026 and 2027 earnings growth is 32% and 16%. Industrials and Real Estate have the most positive recent revisions, Communication Services and Discretionary the weakest.

Mag 7 earnings are expected to grow 25% in 3Q26 against 22% for the S&P 493. In 2027 this flips to 17% for the S&P 493 against 12% for the Mag 7, largely because of tough comps from one-off non-operating gains. Earlier 1Q/2Q EPS was inflated by non-operating profits from private AI investments.

MS analyst previews are positive but less so than last quarter, with net NTM EPS previews at +21% against +27% in 2Q, and results at +15% against +30% in 2Q. Tech (+38%) and Real Estate (+56%) lead post-print NTM EPS revisions, while Industrials, Materials and Communication Services are neutral.

MS Fresh Money Buy List averages 20.0% to price target. Current list average absolute return since inclusion is 48.77% and relative return is 9.39%. Names are ABBV, AMT, CNP, DAL, EQT, KNX, NOC, TEAM, TGT and WMT.
Margins: LTM EBIT margin is 20.2%, expected at 20.6% for FY2026 and 22.8% for FY2027. LTM net margin is 15.8%, projected at 16.2% for FY2026 and 17.2% for FY2027. Semis margins lead sector expansion.
MS forecast table (current S&P 500 at 7,580): bear case 5,900 (-22%), base case 8,300 (+9%), bull case 9,400 (+24%), with a current P/E of 18.7x. Top-down EPS base is $339 for 2026 and $380 for 2027.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS surprise is 3.9% with 297 of 493 companies reported, against a historical average of 4.4% and well below the 2Q26 surprise of +26%. Sales surprise is 2.0% against a 1.3% historical average. These are reported results versus consensus.

3Q26 S&P 500 blended EPS growth is +36.3% y/y and revenue growth is +13.9% y/y on the reported and estimated mix. Consensus EPS growth for the quarter is +28% y/y and consensus sales growth is +12% y/y.
Calendar 2026 and 2027 consensus EPS growth is 32% and 16%. Consensus sales growth is 12% for 2026 and 8% for 2027.

Mag 7 net income is expected to grow 25% in 3Q26 against 22% for the S&P 493. For 2027 the S&P 493 is expected to grow 17% against 12% for the Mag 7, largely on difficult comps from one-off non-operating income.
Earnings revisions breadth is +7%. 3Q26 estimates for Energy were revised up 133.3% YTD and Semis 46.7% YTD.
Free cash flow surprises are producing larger T+1 price reactions than EPS surprises in 3Q26, and misses are penalized more than usual.

trade_ideas.description: Add risk to quality cyclicals that have de-rated, with Industrials as the top pick, after upcoming clearing events (midterms, liquidity, Quarterly Refunding Announcement) or if the S&P 500 reaches 7100-7300.
trade_ideas.rationale: Quality cyclicals with improving earnings revisions have de-rated and earnings growth should reassert itself as the main driver of returns.
trade_ideas.risk: A final capitulation in crowded areas, tighter liquidity if the TGA drawdown does not ease conditions, and renewed Iran escalation or tariffs after the election.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer the equal-weight S&P 500 over the cap-weighted index and the Russell 2000 as the broadening trade expression.
trade_ideas.rationale: The equal-weight S&P can work with a stabilization in the long end, while the lower quality Russell 2000 needs a bigger decline in rates.

tension_points.bull_case: MS says the correction that began in June is in its final innings, with breadth improving, yields down about 40bp since September and clearing events (midterms, TGA drawdown, Quarterly Refunding) ahead. Post-midterm six-month large-cap returns average about 15%.
tension_points.bear_case: Liquidity may be tighter than the Fed acknowledged, the sentiment indicator is not yet at capitulation levels, crowded areas of the index may still fall, and Iran escalation or tariffs could follow the election.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A TGA drawdown that does not coincide with looser financial conditions across rates and energy, or renewed Iran escalation or new tariffs after the election pushing inflation expectations and long-end yields higher.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh did not double down on his Jackson Hole message, so the Fed has flexibility to pause and financial conditions are doing some of the tightening work.
tension_points.bear_case: The bar for additional liquidity support remains high, since Warsh would not call conditions outright tight and remains focused on inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the expected TGA drawdown does not ease financial conditions, markets may ultimately need more liquidity from the Fed.
